# FIG. 5 - Second embodiment with a pulling element

**View:** Perspective view from above and to the front left, as FIG. 1. Outline line work only; the geometry carries no lettering, the numerals below being added in the annotation pass. The vibration motor and the air-extraction mechanism are omitted.

**Geometry to be drawn**

The covering element 36 is one large plain tile in perspective, as in FIG. 1, filling the lower drawing area. The machine stands on its right-hand part, with open tile to the left.

The machine is one plain rectangular body standing on a band that runs round its underside, the band alone touching the tile, machine and tile being shown schematically, these forms being a depiction convention.

The band meets the underside of the body on the same rectangular run, its front surface facing the viewer as one unbroken strip across the whole width and drawn deep, its depth schematic. Its lower edge meets the tile, and open tile lies in front of the machine.

The rectangular body is drawn broad and tall, its front face turned toward the viewer as a large plain surface. The view being taken from the front left, the body's left-hand end is presented to the viewer, the body and band sharing one continuous outer edge on that side, the right-hand end reading as one boundary edge between the top face and the band.

The flexible pulling element 46 is one long solid elongate body, drawn in outline in the same manner as the machine and the band. Its boundary is two roughly parallel curved lines, which are the two long edges of that one body, together with a short line closing it at its free end. It is not drawn as a single stroke, a single curve, a centre line or a path of any kind, and no single-line depiction of it is intended: the two long edges are required, and they are the outline of one body rather than two separate elements. The body sags over the open tile. It begins where it meets the left-hand side of the machine, that meeting shown schematically with no attachment formation, and runs away to the left, stopping well inside the left-hand limit of the drawing area, where the closing line closes it. Its drawn width is held wide and even along the whole sweep, wide enough for a point to stand well inside it clear of both boundary lines, that width being a depiction convention for this sheet only. The sweep crosses and touches no other line.

Every body on this sheet, including the flexible pulling element 46, is drawn as an outlined body with a closed boundary; no element on this sheet is drawn as a single stroke or single line. The whole of the drawing stands well inside the drawing area.

- The vibration device 10 is the whole machine, the rectangular body with its band. Identified on the outer boundary line at the right-hand end of the body, clear of the flexible pulling element 46.
- The flexible pulling element 46 is that outlined elongate body. Identified well inside it at the lowest point of the sag, midway along the sweep, clear of both boundary lines, of the machine and of the free end. The numeral stands in open tile above the sweep, clear of the numeral 36 and of the machine.
- The covering element 36 is that large plain tile. Identified well inside the open tile in front of the machine, clear of the flexible pulling element 46.

**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 46

/home/nimrod_rotem/patent-search-pilot/data/draft_workspaces/p8/draft/08-detailed-description.md:61:FIG. 5 shows a second embodiment. A flexible pulling element 46 is connected to the vibration device 10. The flexible pulling element 46 is a rope, wire, cable or similar flexible pulling element. The vibration device 10 is translatable over the exposed face 38 by tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46 while the pressure differential is maintained: the operator applies that tension and the vibration device 10 slides on the bearing face 26 in the direction of the applied tension.
/home/nimrod_rotem/patent-search-pilot/data/draft_workspaces/p8/draft/08-detailed-description.md:63:This embodiment gives decoupled control. The flexible pulling element 46 moves the vibration device 10 across the exposed face 38 when the operator applies tension to it. The force holding the vibration device 10 against the covering element 36 is supplied independently, and continuously, by the pressure differential across the base 12. Position is thus controlled by one agency and contact by another: the operator sets where the vibration device 10 is with a small pulling force, while the quality of the vibration coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and is supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46.
/home/nimrod_rotem/patent-search-pilot/data/draft_workspaces/p8/draft/08-detailed-description.md:71:A method of bedding a covering element 36 into bonding material 40 using the vibration device 10 is carried out as follows. The method begins with placing the vibration device 10 on the exposed face 38 of the covering element 36, whereby the bearing face 26 of the perimeter member 24 is brought against the exposed face 38 so that the chamber 22 is bounded by the second side 16, the perimeter member 24 and the exposed face 38, with the clearance 34 remaining, along at least part of the perimeter member 24, between the bearing face 26 and the exposed face 38. It continues with operating the air-extraction mechanism 20 to withdraw air from the chamber 22 at a volumetric extraction rate sufficient to maintain the chamber 22 below atmospheric pressure while ambient air continues to enter the chamber 22 through the clearance 34, the resulting pressure differential holding the vibration device 10 against the covering element 36 without a downward force being required from the operator. It continues with operating the vibration motor 18 and transmitting vibration from the vibration motor 18 to the covering element 36 through the base 12 and the perimeter member 24 to the bearing face 26. It continues with translating the vibration device 10 across the exposed face 38, while the pressure differential is maintained, by sliding the bearing face 26 over the exposed face 38, so that vibration is delivered to successive areas of the covering element 36. The translating may be done by applying tension to the flexible pulling element 46 or by guiding the vibration device 10 with the handle 44.

content.text: The single blocker is resolved. FIG. 5's brief is now 2,451 characters (limit 2,800).

input.summary: The only blocker in the review was the FIG. 5 brief exceeding the 2,800 character limit (reported at 3,312). Both reported failures were the same defect surfaced by two gates: the per sheet geometry/leader/OCR gate and the overall preflight gate, so one sheet needed work, not two. I rewrote the FIG. 5 brief to 2,451 characters. Almost all of the excess came from one over specified paragraph that defined the flexible pulling element 46 as an outlined body bounded by two roughly parallel curved lines with a closing line, prescribed its drawn width, and then repeated a set of negative bans (not a single stroke, not a centre line, not a path). That is exactly the renderer wrangling the drafting rules forbid: a pulling element is to be described as one curved path, and negative linework bans are not permitted. It is now one curved path shown schematically, sagging over the open tile, starting at the left-hand side of the machine with no attachment formation and ending well inside the left-hand limit of the drawing area, with its numeral targeted on the path at the lowest point of the sag. No invention content changed: the machine, band, tile, sag over open tile, schematic connection and the numeral set 10, 36, 46 are all as before. I checked the rest of the workspace and changed nothing else. No other figure brief contains banned negative linework or single stroke language, no draft or figure file contains an em dash, placeholder or drafting note, every numeral on every sheet is in draft/numerals.md and every table entry appears on at least one sheet, and no sheet lists more than seven numerals. The specification, claims and abstract were untouched because nothing in the review bore on them.
reasoning: The review listed two failing gates but one underlying defect: the FIG. 5 brief length. I fixed that sheet and deliberately did not touch the other five, since inventing changes to passing sheets would risk regressions for no gain.

I cut length by deleting the paragraph that specified the flexible pulling element 46 as a two-edged outlined body with a closing line and a held-wide drawn width, plus the sheet-wide statement that no element is drawn as a single stroke. Beyond the character count, that text broke two standing rules: a pulling element is to be described as one curved path rather than by counting outline strokes or as a white-interior strip, and generic negative bans on linework are not allowed. Replacing it with a positive description of one curved path fixes the count and the rule violation together.

The numeral 46 target was rewritten from 'well inside it, clear of both boundary lines' to 'on the path at the lowest point of the sag', which is the correct endpoint style once the element is a path rather than a filled body, and it still distinguishes 46 from the machine and from 36 by keeping the numeral in open tile above the path.

I kept 'shown schematically' on the machine, the band, the tile and the connection because draft/07-drawings.md states that the vibration device, the covering element, the flexible pulling element and the connection are shown schematically in FIG. 5. The figure brief has to match the Brief Description, so I restored the tile to that list when trimming.

No claim, description or numeral change was warranted. The claims recite the clearance 34 between the bearing face 26 and the exposed face 38 with continuous ambient air ingress while the chamber 22 is held below atmospheric pressure, and nothing in this repair touches that; a drawing-length defect is not a reason to reopen claim scope.

figures/FIG-5-SECOND-EMBODIMENT-WITH-A-PULLING-ELEMENT.md: removed the two-parallel-curved-lines outline definition, the closing line, the prescribed drawn width and the negative bans on single-stroke, single-curve, centre-line and path depiction.

input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged this turn. The repair was confined to drawing brief wording for FIG. 5 and altered no claim limitation, no description passage and no citation, so the existing distinction stands as drafted: claim 1 requires the perimeter member to bear on the exposed face while a clearance remains along at least part of the bearing face, so that ambient air enters the chamber continuously through that deliberate leak while the extraction mechanism holds the chamber below atmospheric pressure at a volumetric rate exceeding the ingress, and vibration is transmitted to the covering element through that same bearing face. The suction handling art in prior_art/ seeks a sealed cup, where a leak is the failure mode to be eliminated; the vibrating tile art applies vibration under operator downforce or dead weight. The recited combination uses the leak as the working condition that lets the device slide on the loaded bearing face while the holding force is regenerated continuously, which is why translation under maintained pressure differential is a limitation rather than an add-on. The dependent ladder retains the flexible pulling element 46 embodiment, in which position is controlled by tension while contact force is supplied independently by the pressure differential, and the stirring element 48 embodiment. FIG. 5 continues to depict that decoupled-control embodiment.
